columns.name: CustomerID
columns.description: Unique integer identifier for each customer (not a modeling feature).
columns.rationale: This is the primary identifier for joining back to upstream systems and must not be used as a feature; it is unique per row.

columns.name: Churn
columns.description: Binary target: 1 if the customer churned, 0 if retained.
columns.rationale: The binary label the model must predict: 1 = churned, 0 = retained. Treat this column as the target; do not convert to categorical if your training function expects integers.

columns.name: Tenure
columns.description: Customer tenure in months (can be fractional); 0 means joined within the last month.
columns.rationale: Unit: months. Nulls (231) indicate missing tenure information from source and were intentionally kept; Tenure is highly predictive (new customers churn more), so impute or model missingness rather than arbitrarily setting zeros.

columns.name: PreferredLoginDevice
columns.description: Customer's most-used login device during the observation window ('Computer' or 'Mobile Phone').
columns.rationale: Categorical with two allowed values; standardized during cleaning. No nulls remain; use as a predictor.

columns.name: CityTier
columns.description: City tier coded as an integer (1 = Tier 1, 2 = Tier 2, 3 = Tier 3).
columns.rationale: Integer ordinal (1–3). No nulls; can be used as numeric ordinal or one-hot encoded depending on modeling choice.

columns.name: WarehouseToHome
columns.description: Distance in kilometers from the customer's primary warehouse to their home address.
columns.rationale: Unit: km. Nulls (221) indicate missing distance data; values range 5–127 km. Impute sensibly or include a missing indicator; distance may correlate with delivery friction.

columns.name: PreferredPaymentMode
columns.description: Customer's preferred payment method (Cash on Delivery, Credit Card, Debit Card, E wallet, UPI).
columns.rationale: Categorical with five allowed values (Cash on Delivery, Credit Card, Debit Card, E wallet, UPI); normalized during cleaning. Encode appropriately for models.

columns.name: Gender
columns.description: Customer gender (protected attribute).
columns.rationale: Protected attribute: included for fairness and auditing. Do not use as a predictive feature without explicit business and legal justification.

columns.name: HourSpendOnApp
columns.description: Hours per day the customer spends on the app or website (can be fractional).
columns.rationale: Unit: hours per day. Nulls (230) were kept; range 0–5. Treat as numeric and decide an imputation or a missingness feature.

columns.name: NumberOfDeviceRegistered
columns.description: Count of devices the customer has registered with the service.
columns.rationale: Small integer (1–6). No nulls; use directly as numeric or categorical.

columns.name: PreferedOrderCat
columns.description: Most frequent order category in the last month (e.g., 'Mobile Phone', 'Grocery').
columns.rationale: Categorical with five allowed categories capturing purchase preferences; use suitable encoding.

columns.name: SatisfactionScore
columns.description: Customer satisfaction score on a 1–5 integer scale measured by recent surveys.
columns.rationale: Integer 1–5; no nulls. Consider as ordinal or numeric depending on algorithm.

columns.name: MaritalStatus
columns.description: Customer marital status (protected attribute).
columns.rationale: Protected attribute: included for fairness checks and not to be used as a feature without approval.

columns.name: NumberOfAddress
columns.description: Number of delivery addresses the customer has saved.
columns.rationale: Integer (1–22). No nulls; may reflect engagement and should be used as a numeric predictor.

columns.name: Complain
columns.description: Indicator (0/1) whether the customer raised any complaint in the last month.
columns.rationale: Binary indicator (0/1) of recent complaints; no nulls. Strong predictor for churn; include as a feature.

columns.name: OrderAmountHikeFromlastYear
columns.description: Percent change in order amount versus the same period last year (percentage points).
columns.rationale: Unit: percent (percentage points). Nulls (252) kept; observed range 11–26. Interpret as percentage points (not fraction); missing values should be handled by modeling team.

columns.name: CouponUsed
columns.description: Number of coupons the customer used in the last month.
columns.rationale: Count of coupons used in the last month; nulls (210) indicate missing data. Treat as count and consider missingness informative.

columns.name: OrderCount
columns.description: Number of orders placed by the customer in the last month.
columns.rationale: Number of orders in the last month; nulls (243) were kept. Range 1–16. Impute or model missingness as appropriate.

columns.name: DaySinceLastOrder
columns.description: Days since the customer's most recent order.
columns.rationale: Unit: days. Nulls (288) indicate missing last-order date; range 0–46. Missingness may be predictive of churn.

columns.name: CashbackAmount
columns.description: Average cashback earned by the customer in the last month (USD).
columns.rationale: Unit: USD. No nulls. This is the average cashback in the last month (monetary feature). Values are not in cents; treat as continuous.

assumptions: CashbackAmount is expressed in USD and is the average cashback received in the last calendar month, not cumulative and not cents-based.
OrderAmountHikeFromlastYear is measured in percentage points (e.g., 15 means a 15% increase), not a 0–1 fraction.
The row_count (5073) and sha256 (ef1e1f758009fa575837a3b4b62384c1f3516297d775aa2c10ef796a449073a2) identify this cleaned CSV exactly; use them to verify file identity when reproducing experiments.

Nulls in Tenure, WarehouseToHome, HourSpendOnApp, OrderAmountHikeFromlastYear, CouponUsed, OrderCount, and DaySinceLastOrder were intentionally preserved during cleaning; imputation or null-aware modeling is the modeling team's responsibility.
557 duplicate records were removed during cleaning; duplicates were identical except for CustomerID and were dropped to avoid double-counting customer behavior.
Protected attributes (Gender, MaritalStatus) are included for auditing and fairness checks but should not be used as predictive features without documented justification and approvals.
CustomerID is unique per row and must not be used as a predictive feature. Churn is the label and must be used as the target variable in model training.
